A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InquireBench and InquireMobile. All pages, including appendix prompts, settings, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original InquireBench evaluations, training-stage comparisons, and a human satisfaction study involving approximately 200 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds InquireMobile evaluations on AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL-3B model, SFT-to-GRPO procedure, nine-action space, and format/type/argument rewards remain unchanged. The introduction's new two-step description of identifying inquiry needs and generating queries clarifies the existing mechanism without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds actual evaluation on AndroidControl and GUI-Odyssey, extending coverage to ordinary GUI execution without explicit inquiry requirements. AndroidControl was previously only cited and listed among benchmarks. The bilingual InquireBench coverage and training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GUI-Owl while retaining previous comparators. New Table 3 compares against OS-Genesis-7B, OS-Atlas-7B, and OdysseyAgent; Table 4 compares against Qwen2.5-VL-7B, OS-Genesis-7B, and Aguvis-7B. The human satisfaction comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Type Match and Exact Match metrics, including AndroidControl's Low/High settings. The existing 190-task bilingual evaluation, training budgets, model size, and InquireBench metrics remain unchanged. V2 does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a supplementary assessment addressing whether inquiry training compromises ordinary GUI execution, using the new benchmark comparisons. This check lacks a matched before-and-after training control. Existing stage ablations, reward trajectory, and qualitative case remain unchanged.

E5.justification: There is no change in reported seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical testing. The new benchmark tables continue point-estimate reporting, and the existing human ratings and training-reward plot retain their reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 add substantial results, including InquireMobile's GUI-Odyssey TM/EM scores of 72.37/47.93. Table 2 adds GUI-Owl's average ISR/SR/Score of 1.60%/6.00%/0.69 and changes Mobile-Agent-E/Qwen2.5-VL-72B's English SR from unavailable to zero. InquireMobile's original 52.6% ISR, 7.90% SR, 0.78 score, and 2.25/5 satisfaction remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The GRPO advantage and objective equations move from Section 4.1 to Appendix A without substantive mathematical changes. The reward equation is also unchanged. No new assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and two-stage-method contributions, near-zero baseline inquiry finding, and claimed 46.8-point inquiry improvement. The added evaluations support the work without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets the generic-GUI results as evidence of execution robustness after inquiry training. Section 7 adds specific limitations involving layout changes, overlays, multilingual text, OCR noise, latency, and redundant actions, extending v1's existing discussion of grounding and navigation failures.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future data/model/code release promise with a project-page link. It also omits v1's explicit statement that evaluation uses a Huawei phone instead of simulators, reducing device-specific documentation without establishing an actual device change. Training hyperparameters and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including MobileBench, MobileSteward, AndroidLens, GUI-Odyssey, and Mobile-Agent-v3. Related work gains a brief discussion of long-horizon planning, memory, and robustness limitations. The central positioning around proactive human assistance remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies the pre-action explanation, streamlines several passages, moves the GRPO preliminary subsection to Appendix A, and adds evaluation, limitations, and acknowledgments sections. It also updates authors and affiliations. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is reformatted throughout with different page geometry, typography, and figure/table placement. V2 adds two benchmark tables, expands Table 2, replaces v1's numbered thinking-format Figure 4 with an inline colored example, and substantially rearranges the appendix prompt panels and tables.

improvement.justification: The generic-GUI evaluations and GUI-Owl comparison broaden empirical support, while Section 7 makes failure conditions clearer. These provide a limited overall improvement: the added tables demonstrate ordinary GUI capability but lack a matched 3B before-and-after control and uncertainty reporting to establish preserved performance. New benchmark procedures remain sparsely described, and the original InquireBench findings are unchanged.
